No law in the corpus addresses MWCC's frame-size/local-area accounting independent of register spilling; this session's finding (frame delta is invariant to struct-field-count and decl-order, i.e. NOT explained by any existing law) is itself worth banking as a new observation if a future session resolves the mechanism.
attributes.new_finding_worth_banking: The whole local-area of BOTH target and ours (offset 8 through the saved-GPR base) is NEVER read or written by ANY instruction in either version - carrier.message/status/base/msg2 are all fully register-resident (r27/r28) for their entire lifetime with zero spills. The compiler is nonetheless reserving 20 (target) vs 28 (ours) bytes of completely dead stack space for them, and that reservation total is provably insensitive to (a) whether msg2 is a separate local or a second struct field, and (b) declaration order among the three top-level locals. This means MWCC's frame-size computation happens in an EARLY pass keyed to something other than what was directly tested here (possibly a different accounting of the struct TYPE itself, or something outside the three visible locals entirely). Recommend a future probe try: declaring the struct as a union with a same-size scalar, wrapping the whole function body's null-carrier idiom in a macro matching a sibling fakelib.c function's already-exact analog if one exists, or accepting this as a compiler-internal accounting quirk not resolvable via source shape and pursuing WebFrank once sceOpen's blocking residual also closes (WebFrank is gated matching_build_only and this TU is NonMatching while either function has a residual).
